comment: The faults planted in labs/lab-06-review-a-seeded-board/board/, and what a review row has to name to find each one: a word of its Where cell (lowercased) and its checklist line. src/make_key.py hashes this into data/review-key.json, which the check reads.

faults.what: J4's footprint is Connector_PinHeader_2.00mm:PinHeader_1x03_P2.00mm_Vertical, a header with a 2.00 mm pitch. A USB-UART dongle's jumper wires fit 2.54 mm headers.
uio6 and uio7 cross between RN1 and SW1: switch 7 sets uio7 and switch 8 sets uio6, the reverse of the other six switches and of the silkscreen, which reads uio7 at switch 8.
R1 is 0 ohms, so nothing limits the current from the dongle's TXD into ui[0] of an unpowered chip. BRINGUP.md still describes it as 1 kOhm.
D1's pin 3, the common pin of the SP0502BAHT, is on +3V3 instead of GND, so neither dongle line has a clamp to ground.
BRINGUP.md switches the kit off before the dongle comes off J4, both at the end of the steps and when a reading is wrong, which leaves the powered dongle driving ui[0] of an unpowered chip.
Step 6 of BRINGUP.md measures at TP3, and the board has no TP3: only TP1 and TP2.

Board Setup's minimum text height and thickness are 0.8 mm and 0.1 mm, below JLCPCB's 1.0 mm and 0.15 mm, and the legend "SimProc Pmod" is 0.8 mm high with 0.1 mm strokes, so DRC passes a legend the fab may not print.
J3 is 23.36 mm from J2 instead of 22.86 mm, so the board doesn't fit the demo board's three sockets.
